title: prefetch-staleness-and-eviction-ripple-log
content:
Context:
- Problem: prefetch heuristics sometimes bring in keys that are never reused or are reused after they were evicted -> causes unnecessary memory churn, additional NVMe paging, and surprising latency spikes when eviction ripples across banks.
- Goal: quantify the fraction of prefetches that become stale before reuse ("staleness rate"), measure the downstream eviction ripple effect, and evaluate mitigations (staleness-aware prefetch gating, soft-ttl, and conservative interleaving across banks).

High-level hypotheses:
1) A non-trivial percentage (~10-20%) of prefetches are stale (prefetched but not used before eviction) in mixed PL and chat workloads with bursty prefixes.
2) Stale prefetches increase write/read amplification to NVMe during spillback by ~15-30% and push memory bandwidth up during warmup waves, exacerbating p95/p99 latencies.
3) A cheap per-key staleness score (last-access delta + prefetched_generation) can gate prefetch with <5% hit-rate regression and 8-12% reduction in NVMe traffic.

Methodology / instrumentation:
- Trace level: augment existing request trace with fields: req_id, model, route, prefix_hash, kv_key_id, kv_last_access_ts (ns), kv_prefetch_gen, prefetch_outcome {used|evicted|idle}, eviction_notify_ts, spillback_io_bytes.
- Sampling: record full traces for 1% of requests; aggregate counters at 1s granularity for everything else.
- Benchmarks: run mixed workload (chat-heavy + short completion) and a synthetic news-feed-like workload (long context, many repeated prefixes).
- Baseline stacks: LRU (current), LRU+ttl(soft-ttl), prefetch-gated (staleness score threshold), bank-aware interleave.

Synthetic workload config (repro):
- QPS: 2k steady-state, 6k spikes for 15s every 120s.
- Model: small (trimmed) 13B that exercises KV heavily (seq_len avg 512).
- Prefix reuse distribution: 40% exact repeats within session, 20% session-unique, remainder temporal repeats across sessions (Pareto alpha=1.4).
- Prefetch policy: predictive prefetch for next-2 tokens by default with backoff multiplier 1.0.

Key metric definitions:
- Prefetch staleness rate = (#prefetches where prefetch_outcome==idle or evicted before first use) / total_prefetches.
- Eviction ripple score = average number of additional eviction events in the same bank within 200ms after the triggering eviction.
- NVMe IO amplification = (nvme_bytes_during_warmup_with_prefetch - nvme_bytes_without_prefetch) / nvme_bytes_without_prefetch.

Baseline run (LRU): 2024-12-02 lab run (12h):
- total_prefetches: 1.8M
- prefetch_staleness_rate: 18.9%
- avg_eviction_ripple: 2.1 extra evictions per trigger (bank-local)
- nvme_io_warmup: 74.2 GB (baseline without prefetch: 61.1 GB) -> amplification ~21.5%
- memory_bandwidth_peak_during_warmup: 118 GB/s (sustained 90s window)
- p95 latency: +6.4% vs no-prefetch baseline during spikes; p99 +12.1%

LRU + soft-ttl experiment (ttl=30s): 2024-12-09 (8h):
- prefetches: 1.6M (prefetch suppressed for items with last_access_age > ttl)
- staleness_rate: 13.7% (-27% relative)
- eviction_ripple: 1.6
- nvme_io_warmup: 67.0 GB (amplification ~9.6%)
- memory_bandwidth_peak: 104 GB/s
- p95 latency: +3.2% vs no-prefetch; p99 +6.9%
- notes: modest improvement but increased misses for long-tail prefixes that were reused at 35-60s.

Prefetch-gated by staleness-score (per-key score = min(1, (prefetch_score / (now - last_access + 1ms)))): 2025-01-14 pilot (6h):
- prefetches: 1.45M (-19% vs baseline)
- staleness_rate: 9.8% (-48% relative)
- eviction_ripple: 1.1
- nvme_io_warmup: 62.3 GB (~1.9% above no-prefetch baseline)
- memory_bandwidth_peak: 98 GB/s
- p95 latency: +1.1% vs no-prefetch; p99 +2.0%
- false-negative misses: ~2.7% of prefetched-that-would-have-been-used (i.e., gating suppressed a prefetch that would have been beneficial)
- CPU overhead: additional 0.7% on prefetch decision path (cheap arithmetic + per-key meta check).

Bank-aware conservative interleaving (avoid prefetch into hottest bank and spread across idle banks): combined with staleness-gating run 2025-01-21 (6h):
- prefetches: 1.42M
- staleness_rate: 9.6%
- eviction_ripple: 0.7
- nvme_io_warmup: 60.7 GB (~0.6% below no-prefetch baseline)
- memory_bandwidth_peak: 93 GB/s
- p95 latency: -0.4% (slightly better than no-prefetch), p99 -0.2%
- notes: bank-aware strategy reduced localized oscillation; best tail improvement we saw. Implementation requires per-bank hotness telemetry and prefetch placement policy.

Trace examples (anonymized):
- trace A: req_id=abc123, prefix_hash=0x7f12, prefetch_gen=472, kv_key=k:conv:23f, last_access_ts=1699501123000000000, prefetch_ts=1699501123000500000, used_ts=1699501123019000000 (used after 18.5ms) -> counted as used (not stale).
- trace B: req_id=def456, kv_key=k:embed:9a3, prefetch_gen=481, prefetch_ts=1699501221001000000, eviction_notify=1699501221015000000 -> evicted after 14ms and never used -> stale.

Operational observations / gotchas:
- Clock skew across worker threads made last_access deltas noisy: normalize against node-local monotonic clock.
- Sampling bias: hot keys dominate traces; ensure synthetic runs increase tail mass to see long-tail prefetch behavior.
- Prefetch generation id must be incremented only on model-roll or policy-change to correctly attribute which prefetch caused an eviction.
- Edge case: multi-tenant co-location increases bank-hotness unpredictably; bank-aware placement needs cluster-global view or best-effort heuristics.

Actions / next steps:
- Short term (engineering-friendly): merge staleness-gating prototype behind a flag (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rt/pull/824). Roll out to limited internal clusters for 2 weeks with trace sampling at 5%.
- Observability: add dashboard showing prefetch_staleness_rate, eviction_ripple, nvme_io_by_prefetch_bucket, per-bank warmup_heatmap. Owner: Maya.
- Production safety: implement conservative gating thresholds (start permissive) and a canary that compares application-level quality metrics to detect any regressions from false negatives.
- Longer term: explore ML-based predictor for prefetch scoring using features {time-since-last-use, session-id-entropy, token-prob, model-layer-activation-signal}. Run an offline eval on logged traces.

Open questions / research items:
- Can we get similar gains by only changing placement (bank-aware) rather than gating? Early data suggests both together are additive.
- How does the staleness threshold interact with model sequence length distributions? Need more runs with small 128-256 seqlen models.
- What is the user-visible cost of false-negative gating in production for latency-sensitive routes? We need A/B with real traffic.

Appendix: quick commands used in lab
- start trace collector (node-local): ./rt-trace-collector --sample-rate 0.01 --out /tmp/traces
- aggregate prefetch metrics: python tools/agg_prefetch.py --input /tmp/traces --window 1s --out /tmp/prefetch_summary.csv
- perf hotpath (server binary): sudo perf record -F 200 -g -p $(pidof rt-server) -- sleep 30; sudo perf report -n --no-children
- nvme stats script (per-node): /usr/local/bin/nvme-watcher --interval 1s --metrics bytes_read,bytes_written,iops > nvme.log

Notes to self:
- Keep the gating math simple (few flops) to avoid adding CPU bottlenecks on the hot path.
- Prioritize dashboard and alerting so product teams can correlate quality regressions quickly.

References and related tickets:
- INF-321: Prefetch staleness investigation (this doc).
- PR #824: prototype staleness gating in prefetch pipeline.
- Related: bank-aware prefetch experiments (internal notes) and TTL tuning doc (see confluence reference above).

Status: draft — planning pilot rollout once PR review complete.
